title: sustained-burst-regulator-and-headroom-fidelity-meter
author: Maya S. Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets see two qualitatively different burst behaviors: short microbursts (handled well by existing burst token pools) and sustained elevated throughput from feature launches or workloads with long tails. Current autoscaling and token-bank logic privileges short bursts and either overprovisions or aggressively throttles sustained usage, causing poor p95 latency and customer confusion. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a Sustained Burst Regulator (SBR) inside the autoscaler and a headroom fidelity meter (HFM) exported in telemetry. The SBR provides controlled, fair, time-weighted allowance for sustained elevated throughput per tenant/pool using a reservoir with decay and fidelity windows. The HFM quantifies how accurately configured headroom matches observed sustained demand (a percentile-based fidelity score) and is surfaced to the Console and Canary alerts.

What this change does: - Adds pkg/autoscaler/sustained_regulator.go: core algorithm implementing a reservoir that smooths sustained usage, with parameters for window, decay, and max-sustain-percent-of-reservation. The regulator cooperates with the existing reservation and token bank logic rather than replacing it. - Extends policy_config.go to carry two new knobs: sustained_window_seconds and sustained_allowance_percent. These defaults are conservative and overrideable per-dedicated-pool. - Integrates SBR into the autoscaler reconciliation loop (cmd/controller/main.go -> autoscaler manager) and adds lightweight admission checks so the gateway can apply graceful rejections instead of hard throttles when the reservoir is exhausted. - Telemetry: pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go exports sustained_burst_seconds, sustained_reservoir_level, and headroom_fidelity_percentile (per-tenant tags). Also records sustained_violation_count for SLA telemetry. - Charts: charts/dedicated/values.yaml adds feature flag and default tuning for enterprise customers. - Docs: docs/operational/sustained_burst.md describes behavior, tuning guidance, and runbook steps. - Tests: tests/autoscaler/sustained_regulator_test.go covers edge cases around window boundaries, concurrent increments, and reservoir decay. Performance: algorithm is O(1) per admission check and uses a compact ring buffer for short windows; we measured <1% CPU increase on a medium autoscaler pod in staging with 10k requests/sec.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added and CI run green after micro-optimization to lock-free atomic increment path. - Integration tested in a staging dedicated cluster with two tenants running sustained traffic profiles; observed p95 latency improvements of 12% for the sustained-tenant and only 2% overhead for other tenants. - Gradual rollout plan: feature-flagged on Dedicated release channel, enable in warm pools first, monitor headroom_fidelity_percentile and sustained_violation_count, then flip on for all pools if fidelity > 80% and sustained violations < 1% over 24h.

Backward compatibility: default config keeps current behavior unless admins opt-in to the sustained knobs. The gateway admission step is additive and returns the existing HTTP 429 semantics with a new retry-after header that contains a hint when the request was blocked due to sustained allowance exhaustion.

Related work: follows patterns from ENG-1834 (fair-burst-accountant research spike) and leverages telemetry facades added in ENG-2002.
commits: initial: add sustained regulator algorithm and unit tests
config: expose sustained_window_seconds and sustained_allowance_percent in policy config
integration: hook regulator into autoscaler admission path and gateway token checks
telemetry: register sustained and fidelity metrics, add tags
docs: operational playbook and tuning guidance
perf: reduce allocation in hot path, replace map with fixed-size ring buffer
review_conversation: Liam Chen: Please add more unit coverage around concurrent increments and the decay edge case where window aging should release allowance; also request microbenchmark numbers.
Maya S. Kapoor: Added tests for concurrent increments and included microbenchmarks in PR description. Reworked ringing buffer to avoid per-request allocs.
Rohit Srinivasan: Concerned about multi-tenant fairness; request adding a 'min-guarantee' bypass for tenants with long-standing contracts. Suggest config flag per-tenant.
Maya S. Kapoor: Added per-tenant override option with validation; default remains opt-out. Updated docs to mention billing and SLO implications.
Sara Voss: Telemetry tags look good but we need to ensure cardinality is bounded. Please add pool-level aggregation in addition to tenant tags.
Maya S. Kapoor: Added aggregated metrics (pool) and capped tenant tag cardinality with hashed tenant_id sampling in high-cardinality clusters.
Ethan Morales: Approved after CI signal improved and integration tests validated. Noted one minor nit about logging level which was addressed.
CI: initial pipeline failed on race detector in sustained_regulator_test.go; fixed by switching to atomic ops and re-run. Final CI: pass.
release_notes: Introduce a Sustained Burst Regulator to allow controlled, fair sustained throughput on Dedicated fleets. Exposes headroom_fidelity_percentile and sustained_burst_seconds metrics. Disabled by default; ops can enable and tune per-pool using sustained_window_seconds and sustained_allowance_percent.
notes_for_ops: If you enable the feature flag, monitor telemetry headroom_fidelity_percentile and sustained_violation_count for 24-48h. For tenants on SLAs consider setting min_guarantee_percent to avoid short-term denial during ramp. Docs: docs/operational/sustained_burst.md
risk_assessment: Medium: algorithm is conservative by default. Primary risk is incorrect default tuning causing either increased throttles or small overcommit; mitigated via feature flag, staging validation, and per-tenant overrides.
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off in config, disable hook in autoscaler manager, and re-deploy. Telemetry will show immediate drop in sustained_burst_seconds and fidelity metrics.
testing_summary: Unit tests (new regulator) cover concurrency, decay windows, and boundary conditions. Integration in staging with synthetic sustained profiles showed p95 improvement for sustained tenants and <3% CPU impact on autoscaler pods. Load tests ran at 10k requests/sec for 1 hour with mixed tenants.
operational_impact: Ops: small additional metrics to monitor and one new config block in dedicated values. No DB migrations. No customer-facing API change except enriched Retry-After header when blocked by sustained allowance.
audit_log_entry: merged by Maya S. Kapoor; reviewers: Liam Chen, Rohit Srinivasan, Sara Voss, Ethan Morales; CI: pass; feature-flag: sustained_burst_regulator=true;
notes: Drafted playbook for debugging: start with sustained_violation_count, then check reservoir_level and headroom_fidelity_percentile. If fidelity low, increase sustained_allowance_percent or extend window.
